task.title: Decide whether the pinned Cargo graph and tool evidence can fit the current qualification contract

reads: Pinned Cargo source at c980f4866141969fab6254a680546a277789d6f0 through official raw.githubusercontent.com URLs only.
Metadata-only lstat/readlink for the eight explicitly named installed tool paths.
Existing Oxide contracts and evidence under the declared <=2MiB read budget.
prohibitions_honored: No Cargo/rustc/xcrun/tool execution, build scripts, macros or helper execution.
No tool/SDK/rustlib content read, hashing, otool/version/dyld/query/probe or recursive listing.
No nightly, bootstrap, unstable flags or downloads of executable/dependencies.
No installation, SDK content, credentials, signing keys or issuer activation.
No cache/root mutation/cleanup, consumer edits or Contract010 change.
No implementation or new graph mechanism; original 4-Cargo/45-minute trial stays unstarted.
authority.note: Source inspection and exact named-file metadata only. This is inspection, not use of the unit-graph command or an installer.

timing_and_host.note: Host free space stayed far above the 20 GiB stop. No SSD savings are inferred.

http_404_refusals.note: Absent at this pin; the Cargo library root is src/cargo/lib.rs, acquired within the same pinned commit. No substitute pin used.
Speculative path; absent at this pin. Branch stopped, no substitute.

pinned_source.note: Every acquired path is recorded with size/digest. Missing paths stopped their branch; no different commit or mirror was substituted.

pinned_graph_feasibility.verdict: NO-GO under the unchanged constraints; the planner exists and emits command-specific units, but the only supported way to reach it is the unstable nightly --unit-graph CLI, and every route still executes rustc probes and resolution/download/lock side effects.

evidence: src/doc/src/reference/unstable.md:733-757 documents --unit-graph as unstable and examples the invocation 'cargo +nightly build --unit-graph -Z unstable-options'.

src/cargo/core/features.rs:1476-1505 fail_if_stable_opt_custom_z errors unless -Z unstable-options is set and, on a non-nightly channel, reports that the flag is only available on the nightly channel of Cargo.
src/cargo/util/context/mod.rs:397 sets nightly_features_allowed from the rustc channel; rust-toolchain.toml pins channel 1.97.1 (stable).
supported_stable_cli.conclusion: No supported stable pre-execution CLI provides the unit graph. cargo metadata is stable but is explicitly not equivalent (unstable.md:753-757: features depend on the command/packages/targets and metadata cannot represent cross-dependency-kind feature relationships).

sequence: compile_ws:184 create_bcx(ws, options, &interner, logger) builds the whole front end.
create_bcx:285 RustcTargetData::new(ws, &build_config.requested_kinds) probes rustc before any unit exists.
create_bcx:316 ops::resolve_ws_with_opts(...) resolves the dependency graph, writes/checks the lock and downloads accessible packages.
create_bcx:394 Profiles::new(ws, requested_profile) selects the profile; profiles.validate_packages validates it.
create_bcx:443 UnitGenerator { ... } + generate_root_units() select command-specific root units, features and crate types; resolved_features comes from the resolver.
create_bcx:493 build_unit_dependencies(...) walks the resolver graph and constructs the dependency edges and every non-root Unit.
create_bcx:526 rebuild_unit_graph_shared(...) merges/dedupes host and artifact units; after this the graph is immutable.
create_bcx:660 BuildContext::new(...) collects roots, unit_graph, unit_to_index and target data into bcx.

compile_ws:188-191 if build_config.unit_graph { unit_graph::emit_serialized_unit_graph(&bcx.roots, &bcx.unit_graph, ws.gctx())?; return Compilation::new(&bcx); } emits JSON and returns BEFORE BuildRunner::new (compile_ws:193) and build_runner.compile(exec).
command_selected_unit_construction.units_carry: src/cargo/core/compiler/unit_graph.rs SerializedUnit: pkg_id, target, profile, platform (CompileKind), mode, features, is_std, dependencies[]. public/noprelude/nounused are populated only when gctx.nightly_features_allowed (unit_graph.rs emit_serialized_unit_graph).
command_selected_unit_construction.pre_execution_is_not_nonexecuting: The emit returns before the compiler queue, but create_bcx has already executed external work.

rustc_probes.observed: Invokes rustc with --print=file-names, --print=sysroot, --print=split-debuginfo, --print=crate-name and --print=cfg (and --print=target-spec-json for unstable targets) through rustc.workspace_process(); RustcTargetData::new:953 runs this for host and each requested kind.
rustc_probes.consequence: A truly nonexecuting producer cannot be installed: the pinned planner consults the installed rustc before units exist.

config_reads_and_resolution.observed: Reads the config hierarchy, manifests and Cargo.lock; resolve_with_registry:370 calls ops::write_pkg_lockfile(ws, &mut resolve) when not ephemeral; resolve_ws_with_opts:274 calls pkg_set.download_accessible(...).
config_reads_and_resolution.consequence: Running --unit-graph can update Cargo.lock, update/consult the registry index and download crate sources. It is not read-only.

construction_side_effects.target_dir_and_output: compile_ws returns before crate::core::gc::auto_gc (mod.rs:192) and before BuildRunner::new (Layout/target dir). The only output write is the JSON graph on stdout (unit_graph.rs emit uses gctx.shell().print_json). The original 45-minute trial and any build are not executed by this task.

public_api_vs_embedding.public_stable_api: None for the graph. The stable CLI is cargo metadata, which the pinned reference explicitly says cannot express command-specific/cross-kind feature relationships.
public_api_vs_embedding.source_pinned_internal_surface: The pinned source exposes pub fn create_bcx (ops::cargo_compile) and pub fn emit_serialized_unit_graph plus pub mod unit_graph, but the cargo crate is not a supported stable embedding library and these functions consume internal types (Workspace, BuildContext, UnitInterner, RustcTargetData). Reaching them without the unstable CLI means vendoring/forking pinned Cargo as a library.

smallest_scope_and_maintenance_cost.option_workflow_unstable_route: Smallest shipped-feature route: allow the consumer's real Cargo invocation to add --unit-graph under an explicitly approved nightly toolchain or -Z unstable-options (RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP) and capture stdout before the build. Cost: a changed workflow/toolchain channel and a new unstable-flag decision; still executes rustc probes and resolution/downloads, so it must run inside the consumer's bounded acquisition scope, not as an Oxide-free producer.
smallest_scope_and_maintenance_cost.option_pinned_embedding: Vendor/copy pinned Cargo c980f4866 as a library and call create_bcx + emit_serialized_unit_graph. Cost: a fork/embedded copy tracking internal, unstable APIs across upstream changes; still executes rustc probes and resolution. Larger maintenance surface than a flag route.
smallest_scope_and_maintenance_cost.no_wrapper_chain: A new wrapper or a feature-resolver reimplementation is not justified; it would be a new mechanism to review.

unit_graph_insufficiency: UnitGraph JSON provides units/features/profile/platform/dependencies only; it does not provide audited behavior, consuming anchors or native associations.
It does not supply the authenticated issuer, native C/header closure, installation provenance or no-replacement evidence.
It undercounts or omits what the registered boundary cannot map: proc-macro/helper closure and generated/native inputs need explicit associations.

tool_metadata_fit.verdict: NO-GO under the unchanged 16 MiB/file evidence bound: two required executables, cargo (31,867,672 B, 30.39 MiB) and clang (124,676,976 B, 118.90 MiB), exceed 16 MiB conclusively before any content read. The cc symlink resolves to the oversized clang.

unchanged_bound.runner_limits_source: src/registered.rs Limits::NUCLEUS: file_bytes 16 MiB, collection_bytes 256 MiB, associations 32768, depth 32 (src/registered.rs:62-74).

runner_verification_semantics_source: src/registered.rs:990-1090 verifies an ImmutableClass::ToolSdk manifest by requiring complete-root membership: membership(&manifest.root, limits, true, ...) must equal every manifest file plus every directory, then each file is hashed with budget.file (src/registered.rs:554-573), which reads the whole file bounded by limits.file_bytes and refuses Budget beyond 16 MiB.
src/registered.rs:638-683 membership walks the whole root, refuses symlinks and special entries and caps visits at limits.associations (32768).
src/registered.rs:1045 and :1072 distinguish ImmutableClass::ToolSdk from Registry and hash the manifest argv.executable when the verified path is the executable.
src/registered/archive.rs:570,660,791,933 apply the same limits.file_bytes ceiling to decoded/extracted members.
additional_constraints: Per-file 16 MiB is only the first wall: a ToolSdk manifest also needs an exact complete-root membership, so a hypothetical narrow-root receipt still must enumerate the whole rustup toolchain and Xcode toolchain roots and stay inside 256 MiB collection and 32768 entries.
The rustup toolchain and Xcode toolchain roots contain symlinks and far more than 32768 entries, which membership refuses or budgets out.
This small table does not establish whole toolchain/SDK closure or aggregate fit; it only establishes that the two decisive executables fail the per-file cap.
unknowns: Missing required dependency files outside the eight named paths remain unknown and need a later checked scope.
Rustlib/sysroot contents, SDK headers/frameworks and their sizes were not enumerated (outside the named-path budget).

bounded_disposition.combined_recommendation: A concrete supported bounded graph route AND the required input-class fit cannot both be justified. Cargo's pinned planner would give command-specific units, but only through the unstable nightly --unit-graph CLI or an internal fork, and both still execute rustc probes and resolution/download/lock side effects; separately, cargo and clang exceed the unchanged 16 MiB/file ToolSdk bound before content reads. Record the material mechanism-policy choice and STOP rather than adding a wrapper.

material_mechanism_policy_choices.detail: Let the consumer's Cargo invocation emit --unit-graph (approved pinned nightly or -Z unstable-options), captured before the build under consumer acquisition bounds.
material_mechanism_policy_choices.tradeoffs: Uses a shipped Cargo feature and keeps the mechanism replaceable; changes the workflow/toolchain channel and unstable-flag policy; still not nonexecuting.

material_mechanism_policy_choices.detail: Vendor pinned Cargo c980f4866 and call create_bcx + emit_serialized_unit_graph.
material_mechanism_policy_choices.tradeoffs: Avoids nightly; invasive upstream-tracking fork against unstable internal APIs with ongoing maintenance; still executes rustc probes and resolution.

material_mechanism_policy_choices.detail: Admit the oversized required tool binaries (cargo, clang) under an explicitly bounded large-binary class or a raised per-file cap while keeping aggregate/collection and membership bounds.
material_mechanism_policy_choices.tradeoffs: Directly removes the 16 MiB wall for required inputs; weakens the unchanged per-file bound and needs an operator ruling; does not by itself provide the graph.

single_next_mechanism_proposal.proposal: An explicitly different workflow/unstable route: a fresh, scoped pilot that captures the consumer's Cargo --unit-graph (approved pinned nightly or -Z unstable-options) before the build. It is viable only alongside a separate bounded ToolSdk policy ruling for the oversized cargo/clang binaries, which is recorded as a required material choice rather than a second mechanism. No wrapper and no fork is proposed.

bounded_disposition.preserved: Ordinary fresh private validation is retained and unchanged. No benefit, eligibility, reuse or storage-relief claim is made.
bounded_disposition.stop: STOP at this feasibility boundary. Accepted qualification-only issuer and installation-owner no-replacement commitments, actual full-input graph/native closure, final consumer request/settlement/debug and footprint remain required and unestablished.

Exact lstat size/type/device/inode for the eight named tool paths and the cc symlink target.

Whole rustup/Xcode toolchain and SDK closure or aggregate size.

Native C/header closure, proc-macro helper closure and consuming associations.
